s1.where: the greeting page with the writing box at the bottom
s1.expectation: I believe this is the starting page, where one writes a message. It is only a belief.
s1.cue: The words 'Chat with Claude...' in the box at the bottom. The large words in the middle, 'Back at it, Ally Cooper', are a greeting, not a name for the page.

first_pass.why: The big line of text in the middle greets a person; it does not tell me what this page is. If I had been interrupted I would have to piece it together from the box at the bottom.
first_pass.solution: A plain heading at the top, such as 'New message' or 'Start a conversation', in place of the greeting.

test_cases.task: The app opens on the page with the large greeting in the middle and the writing box at the bottom (if it is not already there: open the menu with the three lines at the top left and tap the big word at the top of the menu). Put the phone down, look away and count slowly to ten, then look back at the screen and, before touching anything, say where you are. Then drag the page up and down and watch whether a name for this page shows up anywhere. (The picture with the microphone warning cannot be brought back without the phone's permission prompts, so answer for that picture from this same page.)
test_cases.real_if: you still have to work out where you are from the writing box, and no name for the page appears anywhere
test_cases.not_real_if: you know straight away where you are, or a name for the page shows up
test_cases.persona_report: When I looked back, the large words in the middle said 'Coffee and Claude time?'. They are not the words I saw in the picture ('Back at it, Ally Cooper'). Later the same page said 'Good afternoon, Ally Cooper'. So the one large line changes from visit to visit, and none of its versions is a name for the page. I had to work out where I was from the box at the bottom that says 'Chat with Claude...'. Dragging up and down moved nothing, and no name for the page appeared anywhere.
test_cases.what_they_did: Opened the app on the page with the greeting, looked away and counted to ten, looked back, said where I was, then dragged the page up and down.

s1.closing_comment: Worse than I thought: the big line in the middle is not even the same from one visit to the next, and none of its versions tells me where I am.

s2.where: the side list with Chats, Projects, Code and Artifacts
s2.expectation: A menu has slid out from the left, over something else. I cannot tell which of those parts I am in.
s2.cue: The word 'Claude' at the top, which is only the name of the program, and the list of four words beneath it. Nothing in the list is marked.

first_pass.why: 'Claude' tells me the program, not the place. None of the four items is highlighted, so I cannot tell which one I came from. 'Projects', 'Code' and 'Artifacts' are words I would have to learn here.
first_pass.solution: Mark the current item clearly, with a strong colour and perhaps the word 'You are here', and give the list a heading such as 'Menu'.

test_cases.task: From the page with the greeting, tap the three lines at the top left to open the menu. Say which row, if any, shows the part of the app you came from. Then tap Chats, wait for it to open, open the menu again the same way, and compare.
test_cases.real_if: when opened from the greeting page, no row shows where you came from
test_cases.not_real_if: a row clearly shows where you came from
test_cases.persona_report: Opened from the greeting page, the menu shows Chats, Projects, Code, Artifacts and, below, 'Recents' with two rows both called 'Untitled'. No row is marked. Nothing says where I came from. Opened from the Chats page, the Chats row has a pale grey band behind it. I later noticed the same thing from the Settings page: no row was marked there either.
test_cases.what_they_did: From the greeting page I opened the menu with the three lines, looked for a marked row, then tapped Chats, opened the menu again and compared.

s2.closing_comment: Opened from the greeting page, no row in the menu shows where I came from, just as in the picture.

s3.where: the page with the little ghost and 'Incognito chat'
s3.expectation: I am starting a private conversation, one that is not kept.
s3.cue: The words 'Incognito chat' at the top, and the sentence under the ghost that says these chats stay out of my history.

first_pass.why: 'Incognito' is an ordinary word I know, and the sentence beneath explains it. The heading is rather faint and small, but it is there.

s4.where: the page of prices, Pro and Max
s4.expectation: I am on a page to choose a paid plan.
s4.cue: The large heading 'Get more Claude' and the line 'Choose the plan right for you', with the prices.

first_pass.why: The heading and the line below it together tell me plainly that this is about paying for a plan.

s5.where: the panel 'Add to chat' rising over the greeting page
s5.expectation: A panel has come up from the bottom for adding something to my message: a photograph, a file.
s5.cue: The heading 'Add to chat' at the top of the panel, and the labelled choices Camera, Photos, Files.

first_pass.why: The panel has its own clear heading. If I looked away and came back I would read 'Add to chat' and know what I was doing.

s6.where: the panel 'Select model' with Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku
s6.expectation: A panel for choosing something called a 'model'. I do not know what a model is here.
s6.cue: The heading 'Select model' and the list of names.

first_pass.why: The heading exists, but 'model' is not a word I understand in this sense, and the names Fable, Opus, Sonnet and Haiku are invented. I know I am choosing something, not what.
first_pass.solution: A heading in ordinary words, for example 'Choose which version of the assistant answers you', and plain descriptions first, names second.

test_cases.task: From the page with the greeting, tap the button in the writing box that shows a name like 'Haiku 4.5'. Read the panel that opens and say, in your own words, where you are and what this panel is for. Do not choose anything; close it with the X.
test_cases.real_if: you cannot say where you are or what the panel is for
test_cases.not_real_if: you can say where you are and what the panel is for
test_cases.persona_report: The panel is headed 'Select model'. Reading the lines under each name ('For your toughest challenges', 'For complex work and everyday tasks', 'Most efficient for simpler tasks', 'Fastest for quick answers'), I could work out that I am choosing between kinds of answerer, some quicker and some more capable. I could say what it is for. The word 'model' and the names Fable, Opus, Sonnet and Haiku still mean nothing to me by themselves.
test_cases.what_they_did: From the greeting page I tapped the button showing 'Haiku 4.5', read the panel, and closed it with the X without choosing.

s6.closing_comment: Reading the little descriptions under each name, I can say what the panel is for, though 'model' and the names still mean nothing to me.

s9.where: the side list again, with Chats lightly shaded

first_pass.why: The shading is so pale I nearly missed it. I would not trust it to tell me where I am.
first_pass.solution: A strong, obvious mark on the current item, and a heading for the menu.

test_cases.task: Open the menu (three lines, top left) and tap Chats. When the Chats page is open, open the menu again and, at a normal glance and without studying it, say which row is marked. Then tap Code, and once that page is open, open the menu again and do the same.
test_cases.real_if: you have to look carefully, or cannot see which row is marked
test_cases.not_real_if: the marked row is plain to you at a glance each time
test_cases.persona_report: On the real phone the pale grey band behind 'Chats', and later behind 'Code', was visible at a glance; I did not have to study it. It is still a faint shade rather than a strong mark, and it does not say in words 'you are here'. For me it is usable, but only just.
test_cases.what_they_did: Opened Chats, opened the menu and glanced at it; then tapped Code, opened the menu again and glanced.

s9.closing_comment: On the real phone the pale band behind Chats was visible at a glance; it is faint, but I could use it.

s10.where: the Chats page with the little All / Pinned box open

s10.cue: The heading 'Chats' is still visible at the top. The little box itself has no heading.

first_pass.why: I know the page from its heading, but the small box does not say what it is for. If the phone rang, I would come back and not know why that box was open or what 'Pinned' was choosing.
first_pass.solution: Give the little box a heading of its own, such as 'Show which chats'.

test_cases.task: Open the menu and tap Chats. Tap the small picture at the top right (the one with sliders) so a little box of choices opens. Look away and count to ten, look back, and say where you are and what the little box is choosing. Close the box with the phone's Back button without choosing.
test_cases.real_if: after looking away you cannot tell what the little box is for
test_cases.not_real_if: you can tell where you are and what the box is for
test_cases.persona_report: The heading 'Chats' was still at the top, so I knew the page. The little box said 'All', with a tick, and 'Pinned'. Since the list behind it was my chats, I reasoned that it chooses whether to show all chats or only pinned ones. I could tell, but only by reasoning; the box has no title of its own.
test_cases.what_they_did: Opened Chats, tapped the small sliders picture at the top right so the little box opened, looked away and counted to ten, looked back, and closed the box with Back.

s10.closing_comment: With the Chats heading still there, I could reason out what the little box chooses, though it has no title of its own.

s39.expectation: The page for the voice's settings.
s39.cue: The heading 'Voice settings' at the top.

first_pass.why: The heading is plain. The large card saying 'Buttery' puzzles me, but I know where I am.

s40.expectation: The voice settings page, another voice shown.
s40.cue: The heading 'Voice settings' at the top.

first_pass.why: Same clear heading.

s41.where: the Voice settings page with the long list of languages
s41.expectation: Probably choosing a language for the voice, but the list covers the page.
s41.cue: The top half of the words 'Voice settings', partly cut off by the list. The list has no heading.

first_pass.why: The list sits over the heading and cuts it in half. The list itself does not say what it is for.
first_pass.solution: Give the list its own heading, 'Choose a language', and do not cover the page heading.

test_cases.task: Open the menu and tap the round badge with your initials at the bottom left. On that page tap Voice. On the next page tap the Language row so its list opens. Without choosing anything, say where you are. Press the phone's Back button once to close the list and compare. Do not tap the voice cards at the top.
test_cases.real_if: while the list is open you cannot tell where you are
test_cases.not_real_if: you can still tell where you are while the list is open
test_cases.persona_report: With the list open, the heading 'Voice settings' at the top is half covered by the list, and the list has no title of its own. To its left I could still see the word 'Language' on the row beneath, so I could piece together that I was choosing a language, on something to do with voice. Pressing Back closed the list and the heading was whole again. It is as it looked in the picture.
test_cases.what_they_did: Opened the menu, tapped my initials badge, tapped Voice, tapped the Language row so its list opened, said where I was, pressed Back once, and compared. I did not touch the voice cards. Note: when the page opened it showed a voice called 'Glassy' in the middle; I did not choose that.

s41.closing_comment: The list half-covers the heading and has no title of its own; I pieced it together from 'Language' at the side, as in the picture.

s42.cue: The heading 'Voice settings' at the top.

s44.where: the side list with Code lightly shaded
s44.expectation: The menu from the left. Perhaps I was on 'Code', since that row is faintly shaded.
s44.cue: A pale grey band behind 'Code'. 'Claude' at the top is only the program's name.

first_pass.why: The shading is faint, and 'Code' is not a place I understand in this program.
first_pass.solution: A strong mark on the current item and a heading for the menu.

test_cases.task: Open the menu (three lines, top left) and tap Chats. When the Chats page is open, open the menu again and, at a normal glance and without studying it, say which row is marked. Then tap Code, and once that page is open, open the menu again and do the same.
test_cases.real_if: you have to look carefully, or cannot see which row is marked
test_cases.not_real_if: the marked row is plain to you at a glance each time
test_cases.persona_report: On the real phone the pale grey band behind 'Chats', and later behind 'Code', was visible at a glance; I did not have to study it. It is still a faint shade rather than a strong mark, and it does not say in words 'you are here'. For me it is usable, but only just.
test_cases.what_they_did: Opened Chats, opened the menu and glanced at it; then tapped Code, opened the menu again and glanced.

s44.closing_comment: The pale band behind Code was visible at a glance too; still faint, still not in words, but workable.

s45.where: the Artifacts page with All / Pinned / Yours / Shared box open
s45.expectation: The Artifacts page with a list of choices open.
s45.cue: The heading 'Artifacts'; the box has no heading.

first_pass.why: The page name is a word I cannot learn, and the box is untitled.
first_pass.solution: A plain page heading and a heading on the box.

test_cases.task: Open the menu and tap Artifacts. Read everything on the page and say what you think is kept here. Tap the small word beside the search box, choose Chat, and say where you are; then set it back to All the same way. Tap the small picture at the top right, look at the little box, say what it is choosing, and close it with Back. Finally open the menu, go to Chats, then come back to Artifacts through the menu and say whether you recognise the page.
test_cases.real_if: you cannot tell what this page is, or what the little boxes are choosing, even after reading it
test_cases.not_real_if: after reading it you can tell where you are and what is kept here
test_cases.persona_report: The page says only 'Artifacts you've had with Claude will show up here.' That explains nothing: it uses the same word to explain itself. With 'Chat' chosen it said 'No artifacts match'. The box from the top-right picture offered 'All, Pinned, Yours, Shared with you', so there are two separate 'All's on this one page, choosing different things. When I came back I recognised the page only by reading the heading 'Artifacts' again; I could not tell you what is kept there. On my way back through the menu, my first tap on Chats landed me on the greeting page instead, and I had to try again.
test_cases.what_they_did: Opened Artifacts and read the page; set the word beside the search box to Chat and back to All; opened the small picture at the top right and looked at its box, then closed it; went to Chats through the menu and returned to Artifacts.

s45.closing_comment: This box has its own 'All', separate from the other 'All' beside the search box; two 'All's on one page choosing different things is worse than I thought.

s46.where: the Artifacts page with the blue pin button, 'No artifacts match'
s46.expectation: The Artifacts page, something narrowed down, nothing found.
s46.cue: The heading 'Artifacts', 'All' beside the search box, and a blue circle with a pin at the top right.

first_pass.why: The page name is unfamiliar, and it says 'All' yet nothing matches; the blue pin suggests something else is chosen. I cannot tell what I am looking at.
first_pass.solution: A plain heading and one sentence saying what is being shown.

test_cases.task: Open the menu (three lines, top left) and tap Artifacts. Tap the small picture at the top right and choose Pinned; say which list you are now looking at. Then tap the small word beside the search box and choose Code; say which list you are looking at now. Afterwards put both back: small picture at the top right, choose All; small word beside the search box, choose All.
test_cases.real_if: you cannot tell, from what is written, which list you are looking at
test_cases.not_real_if: what is written tells you plainly which list you are looking at
test_cases.persona_report: After choosing Pinned, the word 'Pinned' appeared nowhere on the page. The small picture turned into a blue circle with a pin in it, and the word beside the search box still said 'All', with 'No artifacts match' in the middle. So the page said 'All' while it was showing only the pinned ones. After choosing Code the word said 'Code' and the blue pin stayed. Nothing in words told me I was looking at pinned items of the Code kind. Two separate controls, one shown only as a picture, and I could not hold them together.
test_cases.what_they_did: Opened Artifacts, tapped the small picture at the top right and chose Pinned, then tapped the small word beside the search box and chose Code. Afterwards I put both back to All, and checked they read All.

s46.closing_comment: The page said 'All' while it was showing only the pinned ones; what is written contradicts what is shown.

s51.expectation: A page called 'Connectors'. I do not know what that means here.

first_pass.solution: A heading in ordinary words, such as 'Link to your other apps'.

test_cases.task: Open the menu and tap the round badge with your initials at the bottom left. On that page tap Connectors. Read the page and say where you are and what it is for. Do not touch the switch or the plus. Go back with the arrow at the top left, then open Connectors again and say whether you recognise it.
test_cases.real_if: you cannot tell where you are or what the page is for, even after reading it
test_cases.not_real_if: after reading it you can tell where you are
test_cases.persona_report: The page heading is 'Connectors', and in the middle it says 'No connectors yet. Connectors let Claude use your apps and tools.' Once I read that sentence I could say what the page is for: joining Claude to my other programs. When I opened it a second time I recognised it, but only by reading that sentence again, not from the heading. A mishap: the first time I tapped my initials badge the settings page opened under my finger, and my second tap turned off the 'Haptic feedback' switch. I noticed it and turned it back on at once; it is on again as before.
test_cases.what_they_did: Opened the menu, tapped my initials badge, tapped Connectors, read the page, went back with the arrow, and opened Connectors again. I did not touch the switch or the plus.

s51.closing_comment: After reading the sentence in the middle I could tell what the page is for, though the heading alone would not have told me.
